latest_release.body:
# Flow v0.1.0-beta4

**Release date:** 2026-11-16
**Status:** Release

Enjoying Flow? Consider supporting its development on [Open Collective](https://opencollective.com/flow-tube) or [Patreon](https://patreon.com/A_EDev) to help keep the app free, open source, ad-free, and improving!

## About

Flow Desktop is a privacy-first YouTube and YouTube Music client - no account, no ads, no analytics, no telemetry. It is the desktop companion to Flow for Android.

## Highlights

- Profiles: up to five people or moods on one computer, each with their own recommendations, history, library and settings.
- Linked devices keep Flow Desktop and Flow for Android in sync all the time, now including notes, saved Shorts and your recommendations, and Play on moves playback between them again.
- Flow Recap: your month, year or all time in videos and music, with a full-window story you can save as an image.
- Videos play in 1440p, 4K and 8K, start at the quality you chose, and switch codec on their own instead of going black. Live streams work again.
- The music player is rebuilt like Android's: a pill mini player that drags up into the full player, Android's crossfade, and lyrics with the Cadence animation, romanization and shareable lyric cards.
- A redesigned search with tabs, one Filters button, richer results and community posts.
- Notes on videos and channels, local media folders, automatic backups that Flow for Android can restore, and imports from Google Takeout, NewPipe, LibreTube and more.
- Flow speaks 33 languages, with right-to-left layouts for Arabic, Persian and Urdu.
- Flow updates itself on macOS too.

## Behavior changes

- macOS: earlier versions were never offered an update, so install this one by hand once. From here on Flow updates itself.
- Linux: the command is now flow-desktop (flow-desktop-beta and flow-desktop-nightly for the other channels), so pin Flow to your dock again. No package installs the flow command any more.
- Remote signature fallback in Settings > Network is now on by default, as on Flow for Android. It never receives the video id.
- The music mini player is now a pill and previous, play and next form one split button. Mini player style and Split buttons in Settings > Music bring back the old look.
- The video title no longer sits above the seek bar outside fullscreen. A single click pauses about a fifth of a second later, so Flow can tell it from a double-click seek.
- Rewinding to before a SponsorBlock segment skips it again. Moving through a queue starts each video from the top.
- FlowNeuro is now called Your taste everywhere, and Trending Region is now Content country, which search and recommendations follow too.
- Scrollbars are hidden throughout the app. Everything still scrolls.
- The Skip silence and Media Cache Limit rows are gone: neither ever did anything here.

## Profiles

- Up to five profiles, each with its own recommendations, history, library, settings and theme. Downloads are shared. Switch from your avatar in the top bar or in Settings > Profiles.
- A new profile starts fresh or copies settings, subscriptions or recommendations. Profiles are not locked, and with two or more Flow can ask who's watching when it opens.
- First-run setup adds Artists and Alerts steps and ends with a summary. Importing a Flow backup during setup now restores everything in it, not only subscriptions.

## Sync

- The Sync page is now a short list: join, start or restore a group, or send to and receive from a nearby device. Once you are in a group, its devices, profiles, recovery words, storage and recent errors sit on one page.
- Choose which profiles sync and what this computer syncs: history, playlists, likes, subscriptions, notes, recommendations and settings. Turn off Sync automatically to sync only when you click Sync now.
- Changes go out about 10 seconds after you make them while another device is reachable. A profile that isn't open catches up when you switch to it.

detail.readme:
**A privacy-respecting YouTube and YouTube Music client with a native, fully local recommendation engine.** Flow Desktop is the desktop companion to [Flow for Android](https://github.com/Flow-Tube/Flow), built with Rust, Tauri, React, and TypeScript.

[**Downloads**](https://github.com/Flow-Tube/Flow-Desktop/releases) · [**Android app**](https://github.com/Flow-Tube/Flow) · [**Community**](https://www.reddit.com/r/Flow_Official/) · [**Support development**](#support--donations)
> Flow Desktop is under active development. Features and storage formats may change before the first stable release. --- ## Features - Native video playback with quality and codec selection, SABR/DASH/HLS support, chapters, subtitles, playback speed, queues, mini-player, and Picture-in-Picture. - YouTube Music home, search, artists, albums, playlists, queue management, synchronized lyrics, repeat, shuffle, and equalizer controls. - A dedicated Shorts feed with comments, descriptions, saved Shorts, looping, auto-next, and timed scrolling modes. - Local subscriptions, playlists, Watch Later, likes, albums, video and music history, Continue Watching, and regional Explore feeds. - Channel pages with videos, Shorts, playlists, community posts, comments, and live chat support. - SponsorBlock, DeArrow, Return YouTube Dislike, and Discord Rich Presence integrations. - Imports from Flow backups, Google Takeout, NewPipe, LibreTube, FreeTube, and OPML. ### FlowNeuro FlowNeuro is Flow's native local recommendation engine. It learns from watches, skips, likes, dislikes, searches, topic preferences, and creator affinity, and ranks content on your device without sending a recommendation profile to a Flow server. The Control Center lets you inspect topic weights, time-based patterns, channel memory, learning activity, and blocked content. You can export, import, reset, or temporarily pause learning with Deep Flow mode. --- ## Privacy and security - No Google account is required, and Flow contains no advertising or analytics SDK. - History, settings, library data, and recommendation state are stored locally in SQLite. - Tauri permissions are restricted to the main window and the OS, dialog, and external-link capabilities the app uses. - A strict Content Security Policy blocks arbitrary scripts, frames, objects, and remote application code. - Rust validates search terms, video IDs, channel IDs, browse IDs, and continuation tokens before network requests. - Media is relayed through a tokenized loopback-only proxy instead of exposing a public local server. - BotGuard and PO-token handling run through a native hidden WebView, with a packaged Node script retained only as a compatibility fallback. Flow still contacts YouTube and optional services such as SponsorBlock, DeArrow, Return YouTube Dislike, and configured lyrics providers when their features are used. --- ## Downloads and supported systems Release builds are published through [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/Flow-Tube/Flow-Desktop/releases). - **Stable:** reviewed releases intended for normal use. - **Beta / RC:** public GitHub prereleases for wider testing. These install as **Flow Beta** with isolated application data. - **Nightly:** automatic snapshots from `main`. These install as **Flow Nightly**, use isolated data, and may be unstable. Download the latest packages from the [Nightly release](https://github.com/Flow-Tube/Flow-Desktop/releases/tag/nightly), which every new build replaces. | Platform | Supported versions | Architectures | Packages | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Windows | Windows 10 22H2, Windows 11 | x64, ARM64 | NSIS installer | | macOS | macOS 13 Ventura or later | Intel x64, Apple Silicon | DMG | | Linux | Ubuntu 22.04+, Debian 12+, and comparable modern distributions | x64, ARM64 | AppImage, `.deb`, `.rpm`, Flatpak ([FlatPark](https://flatpark.org/apps/io.github.aedev.flow.desktop/)) | Linux builds require a compatible glibc, GTK 3, and WebKitGTK 4.1 environment. Legacy 32-bit systems are not supported. See [docs/LINUX.md](docs/LINUX.md) for which package to pick, graphics problems, codecs, sync and moving from Beta to Stable. ### Opening Flow on macOS Flow isn't signed with an Apple Developer ID or notarized yet, so the first launch is blocked with a message such as "Apple could not verify Flow is free of malware" or "Flow is damaged and can't be opened". To open it: 1. Open the DMG and drag Flow into your Applications folder. Flow can only update itself from there. 2. In Terminal, remove the download mark macOS puts on the app: ```sh xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Flow.app ``` For a Beta or Nightly build, use `"/Applications/Flow Beta.app"` or `"/Applications/Flow Nightly.app"`, with the quotes. 3. Open Flow as usual. Without Terminal: try to open Flow once, then go to **System Settings > Privacy & Security**, scroll down to the message about Flow and click **Open Anyway**. Updates Flow installs itself don't need this again. ### Flatpak (FlatPark) [FlatPark](https://flatpark.org/apps/io.github.aedev.flow.desktop/) offers Flow as a Flatpak. It downloads the official `.deb` from this repository's releases, unmodified, at install time, and runs it on the GNOME runtime with its codecs, so H.264, VP9 and AV1 all play. Updates come through Flatpak; Flow's own updater stays off there. ```sh flatpak remote-add --if-not-exists flatpark https://dl.flatpark.org/flatpark.flatpakrepo flatpak install flatpark io.github.aedev.flow.desktop ``` FlatPark follows the latest GitHub release, betas included, and not the nightly builds. The packaging lives in the [FlatPark registry](https://github.com/flatpark/flatpark/tree/main/registry/io.github.aedev.flow.desktop), where packaging issues go. ### Linux media codecs On Linux, video decoding goes through WebKitGTK and the system GStreamer plugins (Windows and macOS ship their own decoders). If audio plays but video stays frozen on a spinner, a video decoder is missing. - **AppImage** — bundles the required GStreamer codec plugins (including `gst-libav` for H.264); no system codec packages are needed. - **`.deb`** — declares the codec plugins as dependencies. Install with `sudo apt install ./Flow_*.deb` so they are pulled in automatically. - **`.rpm`** — the freely licensed plugins are hard dependencies. On Fedora, a full H.264 decoder is only available through [RPM Fusion](https://rpmfusion.org/Configuration) for patent reasons (Fedora's own OpenH264 can't decode most YouTube video): enable RPM Fusion and run `sudo dnf swap ffmpeg-free ffmpeg --allowerasing` and `sudo dnf install gstreamer1-plugin-libav`, or use the AppImage instead. Without it, Flow plays VP9, which Fedora always has. ### Linux startup crashes and blank windows If the app opens to a blank or white window, that is usually the WebKitGTK DMABUF renderer failing on your graphics stack (common with NVIDIA proprietary drivers and some Wayland sessions). Flow disables it automatically and, if a launch still fails to render, **escalates GPU workarounds on the next launch on its own**: first forcing software compositing (`WEBKIT_DISABLE_COMPOSITING_MODE=1`), then falling back to X11/XWayland (`GDK_BACKEND=x11`). A clean launch resets this. You can still override any of these yourself — for example `WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=0` to re-enable the DMABUF renderer. If the app aborts on startup with `Could not create default EGL display: EGL_BAD_PARAMETER` (seen on some Arch-family / Mesa systems with the **AppImage**), that is a known Tauri AppImage packaging issue: a bundled `libwayland` client library conflicts with your system's newer Mesa/EGL stack. As an interim workaround, delete the bundled Wayland libraries and run the extracted app: ```sh ./Flow_*_linux_amd64.AppImage --appimage-extract rm squashfs-root/usr/lib/*wayland*so* ./squashfs-root/AppRun ``` The `.deb`, `.rpm` and the FlatPark Flatpak use the system's or the runtime's own libraries and avoid this class of issue; prefer those when the AppImage fails. --- ## Development Requirements: Node.js 22.12+, pnpm 11.9+, stable Rust, and the [Tauri 2 prerequisites](https://v2.tauri.app/start/prerequisites/) for your operating system. ```sh pnpm install --frozen-lockfile pnpm tauri dev ``` Build packages for the current operating system: ```sh pnpm test pnpm build pnpm tauri build ``` Windows, Linux, and macOS packages are built natively by the GitHub Actions release workflow. Production macOS and Windows releases should be signed and, on macOS, notarized before publication. --- ## Support & donations Flow is free and open-source software maintained by an independent developer. Patreon supports card, PayPal, Apple Pay, recurring support, and one-time tips. You can also donate directly with crypto. Scan a QR code using a compatible wallet, or click it where custom wallet links are supported. The address and network are printed below every code — always verify both before sending.
